content: 1. Interaction with Ferric Derisomaltose: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate reduce the absorption of ferric derisomaltose in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To minimize this effect, iron products should be administered at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after each dose of magnesium-containing agents. Close monitoring of therapy is recommended. 2. Interaction with Ferric Gluconate: The combination of sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate decreases the absorption of ferric gluconate in the GI tract. This interaction is specific to oral formulations. Adjust therapy as needed and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents to avoid chelation. 3. Interaction with Ferric Maltol: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate reduce the absorption of ferric maltol in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. Iron products should be administered at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents. 4. Interaction with Ferric Pyrophosphate Dialysate: The absorption of ferric pyrophosphate dialysate is inhibited by sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate. This interaction is limited to oral forms. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents. 5. Interaction with Ferric Pyrophosphate IV: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate reduce the absorption of ferric pyrophosphate IV in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents. 6. Interaction with Ferrous Fumarate: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate decrease the absorption of ferrous fumarate in the GI tract. This interaction is specific to oral forms. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents. 7. Interaction with Ferrous Gluconate: The absorption of ferrous gluconate is reduced by sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents. 8. Interaction with Ferrous Sulfate: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate inhibit the absorption of ferrous sulfate in the GI tract. This interaction is limited to oral forms. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents. 9. Interaction with Ferumoxytol: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate reduce the absorption of ferumoxytol in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents. 10. Interaction with Fludrocortisone: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate increase the toxicity of fludrocortisone. This is due to the potential for fluid and electrolyte imbalances, which may elevate the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Interaction with Fluoxetine: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate enhance the effects of fluoxetine through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely for signs of seizures, particularly when bowel preparations are used alongside medications that lower the seizure threshold. 12. Interaction with Fluphenazine: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate increase the effects of fluphenazine through an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely for enhanced central nervous system (CNS) depression, especially when higher doses of magnesium sulfate are used with CNS depressants. 13. Interaction with Flurbiprofen: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate increase the toxicity of flurbiprofen. This is likely due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, which may heighten the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Interaction with Gabapentin: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate reduce the absorption of gabapentin in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Administer gabapentin at least 2 hours after each dose of magnesium-containing agents to avoid chelation. Monitor therapy closely. 15. Interaction with Gemifloxacin: Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate decrease the absorption of gemifloxacin in the GI tract. This interaction is specific to oral forms. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents to avoid chelation. Monitor therapy closely.
